title: Week 9 Mastery Quiz · Parties and Electoral Systems

questions.question: In a fictional election, List A wins 39% of votes and 60% of seats under plurality rules. What is the justified inference?
options: The seat share exceeds the vote share; district results and rules must be examined before explaining why
A gap between national votes and seats necessarily establishes deliberate falsification.
The 39% vote share means List A won 39% of electoral districts.
Plurality rules necessarily allocate seats in exact proportion to national vote totals.
questions.explanation: The seat share exceeds the vote share; district results and rules must be examined before explaining why

questions.question: A proportional assembly has 100 seats and a 5% legal threshold. Party C wins 4% of the vote. What should an analyst investigate?
options: Whether votes below the threshold affect seat allocation under the specified electoral formula
Whether the party won a presidential election
questions.explanation: Whether votes below the threshold affect seat allocation under the specified electoral formula

questions.question: Two fictional districts each elect one member, but one contains twice as many eligible voters. Which question is most directly raised?
options: Whether representation is equally apportioned per eligible voter
Whether the constitution has a flag
questions.explanation: Whether representation is equally apportioned per eligible voter

questions.question: Simulated returns: Party X wins 46 seats, Y wins 34, Z wins 20 in a 100-seat chamber. Which coalition can reach a majority?
options: X and Z together, assuming simple majority requires 51 seats
questions.explanation: X and Z together, assuming simple majority requires 51 seats

questions.question: A party claims a mixed-member system is fully proportional based only on its name. Which evidence is essential?
options: Seat allocation formula, compensatory rules, thresholds, and actual votes-to-seats results
questions.explanation: Seat allocation formula, compensatory rules, thresholds, and actual votes-to-seats results

questions.question: A constituency map changes after a census. What evidence best tests whether changes unfairly advantage a party?
options: Population equivalence, boundary criteria, historical returns, and counterfactual plans
questions.explanation: Population equivalence, boundary criteria, historical returns, and counterfactual plans

questions.question: Two countries use the same electoral formula but very different district magnitudes. What comparison is warranted?
options: Measure how district size changes the effective thresholds and representation
questions.explanation: Measure how district size changes the effective thresholds and representation

questions.question: A fictional party receives 12% nationally but zero seats in a district system. Which statement is defensible?
options: Geographic vote distribution and district rules can produce this outcome
questions.explanation: Geographic vote distribution and district rules can produce this outcome

questions.question: A proposal would replace a first-past-the-post system with ranked voting. Which evaluation goes beyond slogans?
options: Model ballots and transfer rules using transparent illustrative returns, then discuss limits
Assume reform alone guarantees greater trust
questions.explanation: Model ballots and transfer rules using transparent illustrative returns, then discuss limits

questions.question: A coalition agreement promises legislative oversight but omits enforcement. What should a senior examine?
options: Committees' legal powers, information access, compliance, and observed oversight
questions.explanation: Committees' legal powers, information access, compliance, and observed oversight

shortResponse: How do electoral rules shape parties, representation, coalition building, and accountability?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
